title: The Young Cowherd's Sudden Wisdom (TA)
summary: A village boy settles a complex legal dispute between two farmers using a mound of dirt. Akbar and Birbal discover the 'Throne of Vikramaditya.'
full_text:
While traveling near Ujjain, Emperor Akbar and Birbal observed a group of village children playing under a banyan tree. A twelve-year-old cowherd boy named Madho was sitting atop a high earthen mound, acting as the 'king,' while two other boys pretended to argue a boundary dispute.

Akbar stopped to watch.

The two boys argued heatedly, but the moment the boy on the mound spoke, his voice took on a strange, majestic dignity, delivering judgments of breathtaking fairness and wisdom!

Akbar was astonished. He decided to test the boy with a real, complex dispute between two wealthy landlords that had deadlocked the imperial courts for six months.

The boy listened to the landlords' complicated testimonies, stroked his chin like an ancient sage, and delivered a brilliant, equitable compromise within ten minutes that left both landlords weeping with gratitude!

Akbar exclaimed in wonder: 'How can an illiterate cowherd boy possess the wisdom of Solomon?'

Birbal climbed the earthen mound and inspected the soil. 'Sire, ancient legends state that King Vikramaditya—the wisest judge in the history of Hindustan—held his court in this very region!'

Birbal ordered royal laborers to dig beneath the earthen mound.

Twelve feet down in the earth, the shovels struck hard stone! Digging carefully, they unearthed a magnificent, ancient marble throne carved with thirty-two celestial angels—the legendary Throne of King Vikramaditya!

Birbal explained with deep reverence:

'Sire, whenever that innocent boy climbed upon this sacred mound, the spirit of ancient justice and impartiality inspired his heart!

'Justice is a divine spirit; when a judge sits upon the seat of judgment free from greed, fear, and bias, truth flows through his lips like mountain water.'

Akbar honored the boy's family and ordered the ancient throne preserved in the imperial archives, reminding all judges of the sacred purity of their calling.
moral: நீதி மற்றும் வாழ்க்கை பாடம்: Wit beats power
